Installing tmux in the guest would satisfy which("tmux") while executing zero L2 tests — the non-evidence plan 1.1 rejects. Closes when the broker ships inside the archive and the guest starts a tmux server; tractable without solving the Windows backend problem, hence the earlier expiry.

the WSL2 leg runs a prebuilt nextest archive: the guest has no cargo or rustc, and its /bin/sh is dash. A suite that shells out to `cargo` or a `just` recipe therefore cannot run here, however its binaries got into the archive. Installing a toolchain in the guest would defeat the archive design the leg exists to exercise.
